- Good Will Hunting

This line captures a perspective on love that I find immensely meaningful. Perhaps the idea of finding someone perfect was never really about finding someone without flaws, struggles, or imperfections. Perhaps it has always been about finding someone whose imperfections fit with our own.

My Take?

I am not idealistic enough to believe I deserve perfection and nothing less than perfection. And I am not realistic enough to settle for something that doesn't even remotely resemble "okay."

As chaotic as I am, and as chaotic as my life is, I want someone who helps me find peace, not someone who adds to the noise.

That doesn't mean she has to be perfect. It doesn't mean she can't have struggles, flaws, or chaos of her own. It simply means that our chaos should complement, not amplify each other.

When two storms spinning in the same direction collide, they grow into something even more destructive, causing havoc around everything they touch. But when two storms spinning in opposite directions meet, they can mend each other in a way. They create a balance, helping each other settle down.

I guess that's the kind of "perfection" I seek in a potential partner. Not the absence of chaos, but the ability to bring each other peace.

And I think that's something every one of us deserves.

Thank you for reading. 🙏
